name: Genetic Frontotemporal Degeneration with Dementia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Behavioural Variant Frontotemporal Dementia Criteria Consortium (FTDC) Criteria

criteria.description: Early behavioral disinhibition such as socially inappropriate behavior or loss of manners
Early apathy or inertia with diminished initiative and motivation
Executive cognitive dysfunction with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial skills in early stages
Presence of pathogenic mutation in known FTD-associated genes (e.g., MAPT, GRN, C9orf72)
Frontal and/or temporal lobe atrophy on MRI or hypometabolism on PET

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive behavioral or cognitive impairment with executive dysfunction plus either genetic confirmation or supportive neuroimaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of dementia and consideration of family history.

pathognomonic.notes: Impairment in planning, judgment, and problem-solving

searchTerms: shrinkage of frontal and temporal brain areas
brain tissue loss in front and side lobes

common.notes: Marked reduction in motivation and initiative
Progressive difficulty in speech production or comprehension

common.symptomName: Memory impairment (relative sparing in early stages)
common.notes: Memory deficits usually less prominent initially

occasional.notes: Signs such as muscle weakness or fasciculations in some cases
Delusions or hallucinations in rare cases
Altered food preferences and oral exploration

laboratory: CSF biomarkers typically normal or nonspecific
Exclusion of other causes of dementia via metabolic and infectious panels
imaging: MRI showing frontal and/or temporal lobe atrophy
FDG-PET demonstrating hypometabolism in frontal and temporal regions
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in MAPT, GRN, C9orf72 genes
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Electromyography if motor neuron disease features present

distinguishingFeatures: Medial temporal lobe atrophy on imaging
No family history of neurodegenerative disease
Minimal cognitive or behavioral symptoms initially

redFlags: Rapidly progressive dementia with early motor neuron signs
Family history of early-onset dementia or neurodegenerative disease
Early prominent behavioral disinhibition or apathy
references: Bang J, Spina S, Miller BL. Frontotemporal dementia. Lancet. 2015 Sep 26;386(10004):1672-82.
Rascovsky K, et al. Sensitivity of revised diagnostic criteria for the behavioural variant of frontotemporal dementia. Brain. 2011 Sep;134(Pt 9):2456-77.
Rohrer JD, et al. The heritability and genetics of frontotemporal lobar degeneration. Neurology. 2015 Mar 3;84(9):927-34.
